'''Reginald Frederick Chapman''' (2 July 1930 – 2 May 2003) was an English [[Entomology|entomologist]] who later worked at the [[University of Arizona]]. He wrote a landmark textbook on the anatomy and physiology of insects, ''The Insects- Structure and Function'', several editions of which have been published.

Chapman was born in London and received a bachelor's degree in science from [[Queen Mary University of London|Queen Mary College]], London in 1951. After a Ph.D. at [[Birkbeck, University of London|Birkbeck College]], he joined in 1953, the locust control service in East Africa and from 1957 he worked at the [[University of Ghana]], studying [[Tsetse fly|tsetse flies]]. In 1959 he returned to Birkbeck to teach zoology. In 1969 he published ''The Insects- Structure and Function'' which was to go into numerous editions. In 1970 Chapman headed the research division of the [[Anti-Locust Research Centre]] and worked for thirteen years after which he moved to [[University of California, Berkeley]] before moving to the University of Arizona.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Reginald F. Chapman|pages=59–60|author=Stoffolano Jr., J.G. |journal= American Entomologist |year=2004}}</ref>

Chapman was married to his student and research colleague [[Elizabeth Bernays]] and he had two children from a previous marriage. He died at home in Tucson, Arizona.<ref>{{cite book|pages=[https://archive.org/details/encyclopediaento00capi_189/page/n893 830]–831|author=Bernays, Elizabeth A.|chapter=Chapman, Reginald F.|title=Encyclopedia of Entomology|url=https://archive.org/details/encyclopediaento00capi_189|url-access=limited|edition=2|editor=Capinera, J.L.|isbn=9781402062421|year=2008|publisher=Springer}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1146/annurev-ento-011118-111820|pmid=30629895|title=An Unlikely Beginning: A Fortunate Life|journal=Annual Review of Entomology|volume=64|pages=1–13|year=2019|last1=Bernays|first1=Elizabeth A.|doi-access=free}}</ref>
